one_sentence_story: First described by Jules Cotard in 1880 and statistically mapped across 100 cases by German Berrios and R. Luque in 1995, Cotard's nihilistic delusion arises when two brain failures collide: silenced insular interoceptive vitality ('zero inner feeling') plus impaired right-frontal belief checking — and is remarkably reversible with targeted medical care.
so_what_for_you: Respect how deeply our sense of feeling 'real and present' depends on quiet bodily signals (sleep, hydration, metabolic health, and medication safety) — sudden bizarre detachment in an older or ill loved one warrants prompt medical and neurological evaluation, not stigma.
